lessons.title: MOCK - Choosing a Stack or Queue

steps.title: Goal and explanation
steps.body: MOCK ORIGINAL LESSON. A stack removes the most recently added item first: last in, first out (LIFO). A queue removes the earliest waiting item first: first in, first out (FIFO). The same stored items can therefore leave in different orders.

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Add A, then B, then C. In a stack, the next removal returns C because it was added last. In a queue, the next removal returns A because it has waited longest. Both structures then contain two items; their removal rule, rather than their item count, distinguishes them.

steps.title: Guided check
steps.body: Apply the explanation, then inspect the corrective feedback.

steps.title: Explain the rule
steps.body: Keep order and count separate. Enqueue adds one item at the back; dequeue removes one item from the front. After four additions and two valid removals from a previously empty queue, two items remain. A removal from an empty structure is outside this example and must be handled explicitly in real software.

steps.title: Trace the order
steps.body: Arrange the steps using the labeled movement controls.

steps.title: Independent application
steps.body: Use the rule in this new small example.

steps.title: Summary and later review
steps.body: Choose the structure from the required removal rule, then trace its operations. Stack means latest first; queue means earliest first. State empty-structure behavior separately rather than guessing.

questions.prompt: An undo history should return the most recent action first. Which structure matches that rule?

options.feedback: The latest action is the last item added, matching LIFO.
FIFO would return the earliest action, rather than the latest one.

questions.hint: Undo the last action before earlier actions.
questions.explanation: A stack returns the latest stored action first. This is a rule-selection example, not a full undo implementation.

questions.prompt: Order the next three removals from a queue that received A, then B, then C.

options.feedback: A entered first, so FIFO removes it first.
B entered after A and before C.
C entered last and waits until the earlier items leave.

questions.explanation: FIFO preserves the arrival order for these removals: A, B, C.

questions.prompt: An empty queue receives four items, then performs two valid removals. How many items remain?
questions.hint: Each addition increases the count by one; each removal decreases it by one.
questions.explanation: Four additions produce four items. Two removals leave 4 - 2 = 2 items.

questions.prompt: Name the structure that removes the most recently added item first.
questions.explanation: A stack follows last in, first out.

questions.prompt: A queue receives D, E and F, then removes D. How many items remain?
questions.hint: One item leaves the three-item queue.
questions.explanation: E and F remain, so the count is two.

glossary.definition: A structure whose next removal returns the most recently added remaining item.
A structure whose next removal returns the earliest added remaining item.
First in, first out: the earliest waiting item leaves first.
Last in, first out: the most recently added item leaves first.
